document.editionNote: The plan prints no date of its own; its text runs up to the 8.8.2019 submission of the state water-bodies action plan to CPCB and carries time targets to 31.12.2019, pdfinfo shows no CreationDate and a ModDate of 26 November 2019, and the file sits under a November 2019 upload path (uploads/2019/11/2019112659.pdf) on the listing page, which was confirmed to link it on 2026-09-06.
document.template: CPCB model District Environmental Plan under NGT O.A. No. 710-713/2017 (order dated 15.07.2019): a cover, an index and eleven chapters (solid waste, bio-medical waste, plastic waste, C&D waste, polluted river stretches, industrial pollution control, utilization of treated sewage, conservation of water bodies, e-waste, illegal sand mining), each a short preamble followed by a responsibility / plan-of-action / stakeholders table. It carries no demand, supply or deficit water-balance table.
quirks: The plan cites NGT O.A. No. 710-713/2017 dated 15.07.2019 (the District Committee order), not O.A. 360 of 2018 which the Maharashtra plans cite.
The cover carries no page number; from the index onward the printed footer number is one less than the PDF page (index = printed page 1), so printedPage = pdfPage - 1 for every figure.
The plan prints no date of its own; documentDate is the PDF ModDate (pdfinfo shows no CreationDate).
The plan prints no district sewage-generation figure and no district water-body count; the only sewage total (5600 MLD) and the only water-bodies table (90,048) are statewide.

The industrial-pollution action table (printed page 22) says 2 STPs are required and 2 provided in the local bodies, while the treated-sewage chapter (printed page 23) says only Karur Municipality of the two municipalities has an STP (15 MLD); both are recorded as printed.
The treated-sewage chapter's sentence 'The entire municipality is not covered under the UGDS S' breaks off mid-word on printed page 23.

The polluted-river-stretches action table (printed page 19) is a five-column layout; pdftotext interleaves columns on a line, so the FSTP quote is that column's fragment of its line. The table prints 'Priority - I' against the Cauvery stretch (its CPCB class); the action points from that table carry it as their priority since no separate action priority is printed.
Bulleted lines carry a private-use bullet glyph in the text extraction; quotes start after it.
The last page (printed page 32) is scanned: the signature block and parts of the sand-mining table are OCR garble ('mmrng itransporting ldamage').

actionPoints.text: Sewage Management: 1) FSTP, Rs.2.85 Crores, Time Target 31.12.2019; 2) SWT, in-situ treatment, Time Target 31.12.2019; 3) LWTF, Rs.13.0 Lakhs, Time Target 31.10.2019.

E-Flow & Irrigation practices: supplying water to the crops by turn system on a rotational basis; awareness to farmers, with Agriculture and Horticulture Departments, on drip and sprinkler irrigation.
actionPoints.sector: Polluted river stretches (Cauvery): SGWA, PWD-WRD, Forests Dept

actionPoints.text: Flood Plain Zone: after identification and demarcation of FPZ, action will be taken up to evict encroachments; agricultural encroachments found along the Cauvery in 65 places in Manmangalam Taluk.
actionPoints.sector: Polluted river stretches (Cauvery): SGWA, PWD-WRD, Forests Dept

actionPoints.text: To ensure all the TNPCB consented units have provided ETP; functional status of ETPs/STPs; monitoring of treated effluent qualities of ETPs/STPs.
actionPoints.sector: Industrial Pollution Control: implementation and monitoring of treatment system for liquid effluent

actionPoints.text: Karur Municipality shall cover all the entire municipality area under UGDS scheme; sewage received in STP shall be treated to the Discharge standards.
actionPoints.sector: Utilization of treated sewage: collection and treatment of sewage

actionPoints.text: Collection of catchment and lead channel pollution data, sewage disposal contamination data, industrial effluent data and solid, plastic, e-, hazardous and C&D waste data for all water bodies.
actionPoints.sector: Conservation of Water Bodies: general action plan

actionPoints.text: Declaring the Designated Best use of water bodies and ascertain the quality of water as per the standard.
actionPoints.sector: Conservation of Water Bodies: general action plan

actionPoints.text: Deweeding, Desilting, protection of drainage basin, channels, stabilization of earthen bunds and preparing cost estimation.
actionPoints.sector: Conservation of Water Bodies: general action plan

actionPoints.text: Identification of river stretches where there are chances for illegal sand mining; frequent surprise checks there by the Taluk Level Task Force, reporting to the District Level Task Force fortnightly.
actionPoints.sector: Prevention of illegal sand mining: preventing illegal river sand mining

actionPoints.text: To carry out Air Quality Monitoring, Water Quality Monitoring (ground water) & Compost quality in and around processing facilities & dumpsites as per Schedule I & II of SWM Rules, 2016.
actionPoints.sector: Solid Waste Management: air and water quality monitoring of dumpsites and compost quality
